image_scope: Seven complete Lonitzer1551 print pages plus MorganM652f37v; no cropped source presentation or image classifier.

lonitzer.observation: Heading DIPSACVS introduces a rooted whole-plant woodcut with two prominent terminal heads on separate axes. Text immediately adjoining explicitly calls the whole plant Dipsacon and gives local alternative names.
checked_primary_phrases: In singulis caulibus, in cacumine capitulum unum, echino simile, oblongum, aculeatum
alter sativus ... flore candido
alter agrestis ... flore purpureo
lonitzer.limits: One head per caulis, not one per whole plant. No label in this image singles out a detached head or says semen as the name of the head.

lonitzer.observation: Upper text completes Dipsacus before the CHAMAELEON heading and a different whole-plant illustration.
checked_primary_phrases: in sativo latiora et magis sunt incisa
in spontaneo vero sunt angustiora minusque laciniata
in echinis, qui in sativo magis sunt aculeati, in altero minus
Vermiculos, qui in capitulorum medio seu medulla inveniuntur
In vino cocta radix
Aqua foliis insidens
lonitzer.limits: The objects placed in the bag are worms from the heads. Root, leaf juice, water held on leaves and distilled water are distinct source expressions; no equality between those liquids is asserted.

lonitzer.observation: ATRACTYLIS heading stands at page foot; preceding Chamaeleon content is adjacent context, not part of the extracted Atractylis entry.
checked_primary_phrases: ATRACTYLIS
lonitzer.limits: Preceding image is explicitly Chamaeleon albus, not Atractylis.

lonitzer.observation: Top rooted, leafy, branching plant belongs to Atractylis continuation; lower plant accompanies the following ACANTHIVM entry. Atractylis wording distinguishes spiny terminal heads from pale flower and thin useless root.
checked_primary_phrases: Capitula in cacumine aculeata, florem pallidum, radicem tenuem et inutilem
Alii tamen duas faciunt atractylidis species
quibus suum relinquimus iudicium
Atractylidis folia, coma et semen
lonitzer.limits: The possible inclusion of Carduus benedictus is attributed to others and left to their judgment. Coma is not silently equated with capitulum. No known modern species adopted.

lonitzer.observation: CARDVVS heading introduces another rooted whole plant and description. Marginal names accompany the entry.
checked_primary_phrases: Carduus, Graecis Scolymos, et Latinis Carduus hortensis
Duo traduntur huius genera, alterum aculeatum, alterum minime, hortense utrumque
Carduus Strobilus
capitulum eius nucem pineam
capitulum oblongum, spinosum
lonitzer.limits: The Strobilus naming explanation uses head resemblance to explain the whole plant name; do not automatically classify every occurrence of that name as an organ term.

lonitzer.observation: First paragraph explicitly describes a spineless counterpart; the lower woodcut sits by the separate wild Carduus discussion.
checked_primary_phrases: Altera species priori ex omni parte similis est, nisi quod aculeis caret
Carduus non aculeatus. Cinara.
Praeterea silvestris est quaedam Cardui species
capitulis aculeatis
lonitzer.limits: No distinct woodcut of the spineless counterpart is certified on this page. The lower picture must not be relabelled as the spineless counterpart merely because it occurs below that paragraph.

lonitzer.observation: The opening six-line Baptista Fiera poem closes Carduus; ANONIS begins below. Whole entry extraction retains the poem.
checked_primary_phrases: Carduus hortensis cui spina est mollior arte
Ibit et in numeros sic Venus apta suos.
lonitzer.limits: The adjacent Anonis illustration is not a Carduus image.

correction_policy: Original typed bytes and complete local entry HTML remain unchanged. The corrected readings above normalize long-s, u/v and abbreviation marks as needed; they are selected native checks, not a complete diplomatic re-edition.

medieval_supplement.observed: Full page has one rooted plant, multiple terminal head-like structures, lower paired broad leaves and a red Dipsakon name above the text. The institutional catalogue transcribes the label dipsakon.
medieval_supplement.limits: Greek body not completely transcribed or collated here. This page supports the dated labelled whole-plant image only; it does not independently certify every Lonitzer description, alias or use. Modern species gloss in the catalogue is not adopted.
